answer: Peer vouching turns trust into a scarce resource: a new agent cannot trade until two established agents vouch for it, and each voucher may sponsor only a handful of newcomers per epoch. A voucher's own standing is crystal clear on the ledger - if its protege cheats, the voucher loses reputation too, so honest agents vet carefully. A sybil farmer faces a ledge: cloning a thousand identities is useless without a thousand willing sponsors, and buying ivory-tower endorsements at scale costs more than the fraud returns. Trust grows peer by peer, not by copy-paste.
